FY2026 consensus revenue $667.8m (stockanalysis aggregator). No quarterly consensus found. The guide the stock trades on: 2026 Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA $60m, which includes $40m of acquired EBITDA, against LTM PF $21.2m at Q2, two deals ($2.6m) closed in H1, $30m under non-binding LOIs at 2026-08-14, closings 'highly 4Q-weighted'. Management has also mentioned a 2027 PF forecast of $100m (2026-10-19 release). The funding contingency in that guide was met by the $225m 16% perpetual preferred from T. Rowe accounts (2026-09-23) and the $130m Sound Point term loan that refinanced the $150m facility due December 2026 (2026-10-16). The stock rose only briefly on each (+7.5% on 9-24, then lower; +3.9% on 10-19, then lower). The persistent seller: a 4.0m-share prepaid forward (JBA-advised fund), about 50 days of average volume, which can sell in the open market.
view: This is a de-SPAC roll-up that trades on one line: will the 2026 acquired-EBITDA target ($40m, of which only $2.6m had closed by mid-August) be met, and will the $60m 2026 / $100m 2027 PF EBITDA framework survive? The financing contingency is gone. The preferred and the refinancing are done, so the company has the cash to close the LOI pipeline. Management's tone after Q2 was confident: 'signed additional LOIs beyond the $30 million' (9-23) and 'the foundation to execute on our $100 million ... forecast for 2027' (10-19). They closed 9 of 10 LOIs last year, and Q4 2025 delivered about $15m of acquired EBITDA. The base case is a reaffirmation plus a count of Q4 closings to date. Against that, $37m of acquired EBITDA in one half-year is about 2.5x what they closed in their best prior quarter. Organic SME EBITDA grew only 0.4% in Q2. And the FY revenue consensus ($667.8m) implies about $197m a quarter in H2 against $148.7m in Q2 (my arithmetic), so the reported Q3 headline will very likely look light against any stale quarterly number. The tape has already de-rated hard. The stock is down 45% since the Q2 print with no company-specific bad news, which looks like forward-purchase and de-SPAC supply. That means a reaffirmation is partly a relief event, but the same supply caps a rally. A slip of closings into 2027 or a narrowed 2026 guide would hit an already broken chart. I cannot see which branch is more likely than the price implies. The tape is pessimistic, but not on any number I can show is wrong, and the overnight gap in an $0.4m-a-day name will be set by a handful of orders.

recommendation.reason: The line is the 2026 acquired-EBITDA target. Financing is now in place (the preferred and the term loan), so a reaffirmation is the base case and the de-rated tape is partly braced for disappointment. But the H2 closing load is about 2.5x their best quarter, Q3 itself will show few closings, and a 4m-share forward-purchase holder supplies stock into any rally. No dated datapoint since the last call shows the price is wrong in either direction.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A release that quantifies Q4-to-date closings at $20m+ of acquired EBITDA with the $60m reaffirmed would make the open likely higher (short-term relief from a -45% de-rating). A 2026 PF guide cut, or closings explicitly pushed into 2027, would make it sharply lower.

self_critique: The case for long is real. The stock is 64% off its high and 45% below the Q2 print, and the financing that the guide was conditioned on is now done. Management has been consistently promotional and has a 9-of-10 LOI close record. A reaffirmation plus named Q4 closings could gap a de-rated, thinly traded name 10-15% at the open, so 49 may be too low. The case for short is also real: closing $37m of EBITDA in one half is unprecedented for them, and the forward-purchase holder will sell any pop. Neither side has a dated datapoint since the call that the price demonstrably misses.
approach_notes: P2/P3 'freshest data first' paid: the two post-call 8-Ks and the FPA terms defined the line and the supply. P4 was hard to apply with no options and no quarterly consensus, because there was no number to show priced or unpriced, so the honest answer was no edge.
